minutes.headline: Water commissioners set a special meeting for Oct 12 to vote on funding a Hickory Hills well pilot study.
minutes.summary: Commissioners approved prior minutes and a revised personnel policy, then planned how to notify residents about a special meeting on funding a pilot study of the Hickory Hills well. They also discussed rising electric and chemical costs that point to a rate increase, the Mass Ave water main plans, and the clerk-treasurer's water licenses.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of August 23rd and September 6th
Approve the revised employee personal policies and benefits letter

budget_items.what_was_said: On-call pay was described as a weekly rate plus a higher weekend rate, covering well checks and emergency calls.
Board favored the one-year, option three study as giving better design data; consultant to confirm the amount.
Electric spending has risen since 2019 and is projected to run well above last year.
Chemical line carried at a long-stable level is running well above it; staff proposed raising it.
Quick estimate of added revenue needed to cover cost increases, to be refined before setting a rate.
A commissioner opposed a higher minimum charge, favoring higher tiers on heavy users.
Average daily use for the area was given for last quarter and this quarter.

decisions.decision: Special meeting on funding the Hickory Hills pilot study to be held October 12 at 6 p.m., with a regular 4 p.m. meeting before it.
October 12 regular meeting at four o'clock plus special meeting at six; the October 28 meeting is canceled.
Water bill insert about the pilot study to be drafted, with a template due to the bill printer by Friday; bills go out October 1.
Town counsel to draft the warrant article; consultant to confirm the study amount; one-year option favored.
Superintendent authorized to sign the wetlands request for determination for the Mass Ave main project.
Board supports the clerk-treasurer keeping water licenses and training, including joining monthly sampling.
Staff to bring rate options with detailed costs; board does not want a 90 minimum, favors higher tiers.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners set a special meeting for October 12 at 6 p.m. on funding a Hickory Hills well pilot study, after a regular 4 p.m. meeting.
Town counsel is to draft the warrant article, and the consultant is to confirm the study amount; the board favored the one-year option.
Staff will draft a water bill insert about the pilot study, with a template due to the bill printer by Friday; bills go out October 1.
Commissioners discussed rising electric and chemical costs pointing to a rate increase; no rate was set, and staff will bring options with detailed costs.
The superintendent was authorized to sign the wetlands request for the Mass Ave main project, and the board backed the clerk-treasurer keeping water licenses.

why_it_matters: The Hickory Hills pilot study would be paid for through a vote residents will be asked to take, so the October 12 special meeting and the warrant article are where its cost gets decided.
Rising electric and chemical costs bear on the water rate; the board has not set one, and it did not favor a higher minimum charge, so the tier structure may change what heavy users pay.
